::: {#def-covariate .theorem}
## Covariate

The vector $\mathbf{X}_k$ of all mutually equivalent variables, an equivalence class of $\sim$. Writing $X_{ki}$ for the $k$th construct on the $i$th observational unit, the covariate $\mathbf{X}_k$ is the vector of the $X_{ki}$, ordered by unit, and $\mathbf{V}$ can be stated as the matrix of its covariates:

$$
\mathbf{X}_k=\big(X_{k1},\dots,X_{kn}\big)^{T},\qquad \mathbf{V}=\big(\mathbf{X}_1,\dots,\mathbf{X}_K\big).
$$

For scalar constructs, $\mathbf{X}_k\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and $\mathbf{V}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times K}$. When units fall into classes carrying different constructs, $\mathbf{V}$ is one such matrix per class, and its entries may be vectors.
:::
